stem:
A student observes the orbits of some of the moons around the planet Saturn, as shown in Fig. 2.1.

[[fig:f1]]

For the moon Pandora, the period of the orbit and the mean distance from the centre of Saturn are determined.

The measurements of period *T* and mean distance *r* are repeated for other moons.

It is suggested that *T* and *r* are related by the equation

$T = \frac{2\pi r^n}{k}$

where *n* and *k* are constants.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
A graph is plotted of lg *T* on the *y*-axis against lg *r* on the *x*-axis.

Determine expressions for the gradient and *y*-intercept.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text:
Values of *r* and *T* are given for different moons in Table 2.1.

[[fig:f2]]

Calculate and record values of lg (*r* / 10⁸ m) and lg (*T* / 10³ s) in Table 2.1. Include the absolute uncertainties in lg (*T* / 10³ s).

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text:
Plot a graph of lg (*T* / 10³ s) against lg (*r* / 10⁸ m). Include error bars for lg (*T* / 10³ s).

[[fig:f3]]

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Draw the straight line of best fit and a worst acceptable straight line on your graph. Label both lines.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text: Determine the gradient of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Determine the *y*-intercept of the line of best fit. Include the absolute uncertainty in your answer.

parts.label: (d)
parts.text: Using your answers to (a), (c)(iii) and (c)(iv), determine the values of *n* and *k*. Include the absolute uncertainties in *n* and *k*. You need not be concerned with units.

parts.label: (e)
parts.text:
Titan is another moon of Saturn. The orbit of Titan has a period of 1.38 × 10⁶ s.

Determine the value of *r* for Titan.

figures.caption: Fig. 2.1
figures.alt: Diagram of Saturn surrounded by oval orbits labelled with the moons Mimas, Pandora, Enceladus, Dione, Tethys and Rhea.

figures.caption: Table 2.1
figures.alt: Table of moon names and values of r and T, with blank columns for lg (r / 10⁸ m) and lg (T / 10³ s).
Blank graph grid with lg (r / 10⁸ m) on the horizontal axis and lg (T / 10³ s) on the vertical axis.
